data.title: Infinity Bancorp Announces Closing of $7.8 Million Subordinated Note Offering
data.description:
SANTA ANA, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Infinity Bancorp (OTCQB:INFT) (the "Company"), the holding company for Infinity Bank, today announced that it completed a private placement of $7.8 million in aggregate principal amount of subordinated notes (the "Notes"). The offering consisted of $4.4 million of nonconvertible subordinated notes and $3.4 million of convertible subordinated notes.

The Notes mature on December 1, 2036. The Company has the option to redeem these notes beginning in December 2031, subject to applicable regulatory approvals.

The Notes are intended to qualify as Tier 2 regulatory capital. The Company intends to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including support for continued organic growth and strategic initiatives.

The Notes and the common stock issuable upon conversion have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or applicable state securities laws and may not be offered or sold absent registration or an applicable exemption. This release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any securities.

data.title: Capricor Therapeutics Provides Regulatory Update on Deramiocel BLA for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
data.description:
• Company receives Complete Response Letter from FDA for Deramiocel BLA
  • Conference call and webcast Monday, November 23, at 8:30 a.m. ET

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR), a biotechnology company developing transformative cell and exosome-based therapeutics for rare diseases, today announced that it received a Complete Response Letter (CRL) from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for its resubmitted Biologics License Application (BLA) for Deramiocel, its investigational cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). The CRL states that the FDA does not consider the data sufficient to establish substantial evidence of effectiveness and cites certain other clinical deficiencies.

“We are deeply disappointed for the boys and young men living with Duchenne and their families,” said Linda Marbán, Ph.D., Capricor’s Chief Executive Officer. “Deramiocel has been studied in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, HOPE-2 and HOPE-3, both of which met their primary endpoints. We stand behind the rigor of our clinical program and the integrity of our data, and we believe the data support approval. We are reviewing the letter carefully and will share next steps once we have completed our evaluation.”

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities of approximately $198.5 million, which it believes is sufficient to fund its planned operations for at least the next 12 months. The Company is reviewing its operating costs to further extend its cash runway.

Conference Call and Webcast

To participate in the conference call, please dial 1-800-717-1738 (Domestic) or 1-646-307-1865 (International) and reference the conference ID: 27699. Participants may dial in using the numbers above and ask to be joined to the call or click the Call Me™ link for instant telephone access to the event. To participate via a webcast, please click here. A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the conclusion of the live event and will be accessible in the Investors section of the Company’s website.

About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy

Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, X-linked genetic disorder characterized by progressive muscle degeneration affecting the skeletal, respiratory, and cardiac muscles. It is caused by the absence of functional dystrophin, a key structural protein in muscle cells. DMD affects approximately 15,000 individuals in the United States, primarily males. Over time, deterioration of the heart muscle leads to cardiomyopathy and heart failure, the leading cause of death in DMD. There is no cure, and treatment options remain limited.

About Deramiocel

Deramiocel (CAP-1002) consists of allogeneic cardiosphere-derived cells (CDCs), a rare population of cardiac cells that have been shown in preclinical and clinical studies to exert immunomodulatory and anti-fibrotic actions in the preservation of skeletal and cardiac muscle function in muscular dystrophies such as DMD. CDCs act by secreting extracellular vesicles known as exosomes, which target macrophages and alter their expression profile to adopt a healing rather than pro-inflammatory phenotype. For the treatment of DMD, Deramiocel holds Orphan Drug, RMAT and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the U.S., and Orphan Drug and ATMP designations in Europe.

About Capricor Therapeutics

Capricor Therapeutics (NASDAQ: CAPR) is a biotechnology company dedicated to advancing cell and exosome-based therapeutics for the treatment of rare diseases. Our lead product candidate, Deramiocel, is an allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy in late-stage development for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, evaluated in clinical studies for its potential to preserve skeletal and cardiac muscle function. Capricor is also advancing its proprietary StealthX™ exosome platform for the targeted delivery of oligonucleotides, proteins, and small-molecule therapeutics across a range of diseases. At Capricor, we are committed to delivering new therapies for patients with rare diseases. For more information, visit capricor.com and follow Capricor on Facebook, Instagram and X.

Any statements that are not statements of historical fact (including statements containing the words “believes,” “plans,” “could,” “anticipates,” “expects,” “estimates,” “should,” “target,” “will,” “would” and similar expressions) should also be considered to be forward-looking statements. There are a number of important factors that could cause actual results or events to differ materially from those indicated by such forward-looking statements. More information about these and other risks that may impact Capricor’s business is set forth in Capricor’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on March 17, 2026, and in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10, 2026. data.title: /IMAGE UPDATE - Sidus Space, Inc./
data.description:
/IMAGE UPDATE - Sidus Space, Inc./

/IMAGE UPDATE - Sidus Space, Inc./

PR Newswire

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla., Nov. 19, 2026

In the news release, Sidus Space Expands Aerospace Customer Base with Argotec Order, issued 19-Nov-2026 by Sidus Space, Inc. over PR Newswire, we are advised by the company that the image has been updated. The complete, corrected release follows:

Sidus Space Expands Aerospace Customer Base with Argotec Order

Sidus extends nearly 15 years of aerospace manufacturing, proven on its own LizzieSat satellites in orbit, to a new international customer.

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sidus Space, Inc. (NASDAQ: SIDU) ("Sidus" or the "Company"), a vertically integrated space and defense technology systems integrator, today announced it has secured a purchase order from new customer Argotec Group ("Argotec"), an international space company headquartered in Italy, with operations in Germany and the United States, including a technology hub in California and a second production facility in Melbourne, Florida. Under the purchase order, Sidus will manufacture cable assemblies supporting Argotec's HAWK satellite platform, with delivery expected in the first quarter of 2027.

Sidus designs, builds, and operates its own LizzieSat satellites, producing the cable harnesses, structures, and avionics that fly aboard them in its 35,000-square-foot facility in Cape Canaveral, Florida. That work is proven in orbit: LizzieSat-3 is currently hosting HEO USA's non-Earth imaging payload, which is actively capturing imagery. From the same facility, Sidus delivers end to end satellite infrastructure, mission-critical hardware, and technology integration including Fortis VPX – Maxima, an all-domain digital mission computing platform, all designed, built, tested, and operated in-house. Sidus has manufactured aerospace hardware for nearly 15 years and went public as a NASDAQ-listed company in 2021.

"We design and build the cable harnesses that fly on our own spacecraft, and that flight heritage is exactly what we now bring to other satellite manufacturers." said Carol Craig, Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Sidus Space. "Growing space companies need suppliers who have already solved these problems on their own spacecraft, and Argotec is the latest international company to put our experience to work, with U.S. operations just down the coast from our Cape Canaveral facility."

Argotec opened its first U.S. production facility, a Space Factory in Melbourne, Florida, near Kennedy Space Center, with an investment of more than $25 million, followed by the establishment of a technology hub in California dedicated to the development of telecommunications technologies. Both U.S. teams support government and commercial missions and will contribute to the continued growth of Argotec's presence in the United States. The company expects to triple the size of its U.S. teams over the next two years, expanding its capabilities and strengthening partnerships across the U.S. space ecosystem.

About Sidus Space  

Sidus Space®, Inc.  (NASDAQ: SIDU) is a vertically integrated space and defense technology company delivering satellite manufacturing and technology integration across all orbits, including LEO, GEO and lunar; all domain digital mission computing solutions; mission planning and management operations; AI enabling products and services; and space and defense hardware manufacturing. With its mission of Space Access Reimagined®, Sidus Space is committed to rapid innovation, adaptable solutions, and the optimization of space systems and data collection performance. With demonstrated space heritage, including designing, manufacturing and operating its own satellite and sensor system, LizzieSat®, Sidus Space serves government, defense, intelligence, and commercial customers around the globe. Strategically headquartered on Florida's Space Coast, Sidus Space operates a 35,000-square-foot space manufacturing, assembly, integration, and testing facility with direct access to nearby launch facilities. For more information, visit: sidusspace.com

About Argotec

Argotec is a space company with offices in Turin, Germany, and the United States. It specializes in manufacturing high-reliability small satellites and their subsystems for missions in low, medium, and geostationary Earth orbits, serving institutions, international agencies, government bodies, and civil protection authorities. In 2022, Argotec was the only company in the world to have two microsatellites operating in deep space as part of NASA's DART and Artemis I missions. Its current projects include HEO, the Earth observation constellation developed under Italy's IRIDE program; HENON, a mission to study solar storms and other space weather phenomena that can impact terrestrial and orbital critical infrastructure; and MiniCOR, a NASA program that will observe coronal mass ejections and the solar wind. Argotec also develops advanced dual-use technologies for inter-satellite cooperation, edge computing, and data intelligence, supporting security and monitoring programs across civil and defense applications. In 2024, Argotec inaugurated SpacePark, its highly automated production facility. In 2026, it opened its U.S. facility in Melbourne, Florida, and established a presence in California focused on telecommunications technologies. In October 2026, Argotec completed a €50 million capital increase through NUO Space S.p.A. The company is a leading player in the international New Space Economy and collaborates with partners worldwide.

data.title: Hodes Milman Launches California Initiative on Missed Breast Cancer Diagnoses
data.description:
Hodes Milman Launches California Initiative on Missed Breast Cancer Diagnoses

Hodes Milman Launches California Initiative on Missed Breast Cancer Diagnoses

PR Newswire

SAN JUAN CAPISTRANO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026

SAN JUAN CAPISTRANO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hodes Milman has launched The Missed Diagnosis Project: California, a statewide initiative examining breast cancer diagnostic failures and helping patients seek answers about unresolved symptoms and imaging results.

"Breast cancer misdiagnosis is not just a legal issue. It is a patient safety failure," said Dan Hodes, founding and managing partner of Hodes Milman. "In the cases we most commonly see, a mammogram or ultrasound shows something that should have prompted further evaluation, but the finding is read as benign. In others, a patient reports a lump or other symptom and does not get the imaging or biopsy she needs in time. Either way, the medical system has a duty to act, and too often patients get reassured, delayed, or lost in the system until the cancer advances."

The project will address misinterpreted scans, delayed referrals and incomplete follow-up, while educating patients about additional testing and second opinions.

"An abnormal mammogram should trigger action, not confusion," Hodes said. "And a mammogram or ultrasound that is read as normal should actually be normal. The danger comes when a suspicious finding is under-called, or when no one clearly tells the patient what the result means, who is responsible for follow-up, or when additional testing needs to happen."

Patients will be encouraged to request their imaging reports, clarify who will order the next test and seek further evaluation when symptoms persist despite reassuring results.

"Patients should not have to become their own safety net," Hodes said. "But until the system improves, women need to know what questions to ask, what records to request, and when a delayed answer — or a reassuring answer that does not match their symptoms — is not good enough."

The initiative will also examine racial disparities and barriers affecting rural patients and women under 50.

"Many breast cancer diagnostic failures do not happen in one dramatic moment," Hodes said. "They happen through a series of missed opportunities. A suspicious imaging finding gets under-called. A recommended MRI never gets ordered. A referral does not get made. A patient gets told to wait. A lump gets dismissed. By the time someone finally acts, the disease may be far more advanced."

About Hodes Milman
Based in Irvine, Hodes Milman represents patients and families in medical malpractice and personal injury cases, including cancer misdiagnosis, surgical errors, birth injuries and wrongful death. Visit www.verdictvictory.com.

data.title: NSSF Challenges Maryland's Unconstitutional Ban on Popular Striker-Fired Handguns
data.description:
NSSF Challenges Maryland's Unconstitutional Ban on Popular Striker-Fired Handguns

NSSF Challenges Maryland's Unconstitutional Ban on Popular Striker-Fired Handguns

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NSSF®, The Firearm Industry Trade Association, filed a lawsuit challenging Maryland's ban on popular cruciform-trigger handguns. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore signed S.B. 334 prohibiting the sale of these commonly owned firearms in the state earlier this year. The misguided law unconstitutionally infringes on the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding Maryland residents by prohibiting an entire class of lawfully made and sold handguns.

NSSF is pursuing a challenge to a similar unconstitutional law in Connecticut and recently secured a preliminary injunction barring enforcement of that law before it went into effect.

Maryland's law targeting "convertible pistols" infringes on the right of citizens to purchase the most-popular-selling handguns that are used for self-defense and renowned for their reliability. Maryland is unconstitutionally infringing on Second Amendment rights while ignoring criminals who violate federal and state law to illegally modify these handguns by attaching a "machinegun conversion device," or MCD, which has long been illegal to both make, import, possess or to attach to a firearm outside of strict federal licensing. The firearm industry warns gun owners against illegal modifications that override intentional semiautomatic firearm engineering designs. Illegally modifying a firearm to enable automatic fire is a federal and state crime. NSSF also strongly believes it's the Second Amendment right of firearm industry members suing Maryland to engage in lawful commerce by selling to law-abiding Americans the commonly used firearms they choose to acquire and which are protected by the constitution.

"To borrow on a line from James Carville, whom Democrats revere, 'it's the criminal, stupid,'" said Lawrence G. Keane, NSSF's Senior Vice President & General Counsel. "This law, and similar laws passed in other states, punishes law-abiding citizens by infringing on their Second Amendment rights to legally obtain the firearms they choose to protect themselves and their families against criminals who, by definition, have no respect for life or law. Instead of enforcing the law and holding these criminals accountable, Maryland's elected officials pander to gun control donors and antigun special interests to scapegoat the industry and ban an entire class of ordinary firearms, which the U.S. Supreme Court's Heller decision clearly holds violates the U.S. Constitution. Governor Moore knew this yet didn't hesitate to trample on the Second Amendment."

Under Maryland's S.B. 334, the ban includes pistols with a cruciform trigger bar that Maryland lawmakers say can be readily illegally converted by replacing the slide backplate with an illegal MCD. The ban is set to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

NSSF is joined in this lawsuit by the following NSSF member companies: GLOCK, Inc., Shadow Systems LLC, Sturm, Ruger & Co., Inc., Derya USA, Palmetto State Armory, LLC and Fred's Outdoors, LLC.

NSSF warns gun owners to stay on the "Right Side of LegalTM" when making improvements or customizing firearms. The Firearm Industry Trade Association warns that modifying a firearm by adding an illegal device that overrides the original, intended function or design to render a semiautomatic firearm into an automatic firearm is a felony. That includes importing, possessing, making or selling an MCD. It's a violation of the National Firearms Act (NFA) and carries a prison sentence of up to 10 years and up to $250,000 in fines.

About NSSF
NSSF is the trade association for the firearm industry. Its mission is to promote, protect and preserve hunting and the shooting sports. Formed in 1961, NSSF has a membership of thousands of manufacturers, distributors, firearms retailers, shooting ranges, sportsmen's organizations and publishers nationwide. For more information, visit nssf.org.

data.title: Court Grants Final Approval to Roundup™ Class Settlement
data.description:
Court Grants Final Approval to Roundup™ Class Settlement

  • Class settlement and the U.S. Supreme Court ruling are mutually reinforcing pillars in multi-pronged strategy to significantly contain the litigation
  • Monsanto will continue to vigorously defend cases and apply the Durnell ruling

Today, a Missouri state court granted final approval of the U.S. nationwide class settlement designed to resolve current and future Roundup™ claims alleging non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) injuries through a long-term claims program. The Court’s final approval order is subject to appeal. The class settlement, combined with the U.S. Supreme Court’s favorable ruling in June in the Durnell case, are mutually reinforcing pillars in the company’s multipronged strategy designed to significantly contain the Roundup™ litigation.

“The Court's final approval is a decisive milestone in the company's strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup™ litigation,” said Bill Anderson, CEO at Bayer.

The class approval decision follows closely on the heels of the unanimous defense verdict in Aretino, the first case to go to trial since the U.S. Supreme Court’s Durnell decision. Plaintiffs failed to prove design defect, fraud and negligence claims at trial, after the Court ruled their failure-to-warn claims were preempted by Durnell. This result validates Monsanto’s argument that these claims cannot be proven given that EPA and every other major regulatory body worldwide that has assessed such products, has found they can be used safely and are not carcinogenic. Glyphosate-based herbicides are critical tools that farmers rely on to produce affordable food and feed the world.

The company expects the number of opt outs to be manageable and amount to a very low percentage of current and potential future claims. Further, while a portion of the opt out claimants may pursue claims through the court system, many may not. Any plaintiff who chooses to litigate will face the burdens of both establishing that they have viable claims post-Durnell and ultimately proving them to a judge and jury. Monsanto believes the company is adequately provisioned to manage the remaining litigation.

About the class program

Monsanto pursued the class settlement to significantly contain the litigation, and the settlement agreement does not contain any admission of liability or wrongdoing. The Supreme Court ruling should foreclose any present or future claims based on failure-to-warn theories, the central theory in the litigation to date, including claims by opt outs from the class. The class settlement, in turn, provides a long-term claims program that will resolve present and future NHL injury claims, regardless of the legal theory on which they are based.

To fund the class settlement, Monsanto will make declining capped annual payments for up to 21 years totaling up to 7.25 billion U.S. dollars, inclusive of payments already made. The long-term payment stream will provide both greater certainty and control regarding litigation costs for current claims and future claimants.

The settlement includes plaintiffs who allege exposure to Roundup™ prior to February 17, 2026, and:

  • have a medical diagnosis of NHL now; or
  • receive a medical diagnosis of NHL before the end of a 16-year period following the effective date of the agreement.

Any appeal of the Court’s final approval order would pause further Monsanto payments until such appeals are exhausted. Monsanto believes the Court’s thoughtful and well-reasoned final approval order provides a very strong foundation supporting the class settlement, if the approval order is appealed, and the company will work together with class counsel to defend any challenges.

Find more information at www.bayer.com.

data.title: Mendez & Sanchez Finds Three Counties Accounted for Nearly Two-Thirds of California Rideshare Trips
data.description:
Mendez & Sanchez Finds Three Counties Accounted for Nearly Two-Thirds of California Rideshare Trips

Mendez & Sanchez Finds Three Counties Accounted for Nearly Two-Thirds of California Rideshare Trips

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 20, 2026

The firm's review of 2019–2020 collision and trip data highlights the need for bilingual insurance guidance in California's largest rideshare markets.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A Mendez & Sanchez APC review of California rideshare records found that Los Angeles, San Francisco and San Diego counties accounted for nearly two-thirds of the state's rideshare trips from September 2019 through August 2020. For passengers in Los Angeles and San Diego counties, both home to large Latino communities, the firm says access to bilingual information can make a difference when a crash raises questions about insurance.

"This is not about saying Latino passengers are inherently more likely to be injured in a rideshare crash," said Michael Sanchez, co-founder and managing partner at Mendez & Sanchez APC. "It is about recognizing that rideshare collision exposure is concentrated in counties where millions of Latino and Spanish-speaking residents live, work and use app-based transportation. That makes access to clear legal information in English and Spanish especially important."

The firm reviewed the San Francisco County Transportation Authority's analysis of reports filed by Uber and Lyft. The authority counted nearly 27,000 reported collisions statewide during the 12-month period. Uber reported about 14,800 collisions and Lyft about 11,200. Comparing those figures with subsequent years is difficult because the California Public Utilities Commission suspended the requirement that companies submit public versions of their 2021 through 2024 annual reports.

"Passengers deserve transparency," said Sanchez. "If someone is injured in an Uber or Lyft crash, they should not have to guess what insurance applies, what evidence they need to save or whether they have the right to pursue a claim."

California's Senate Bill 371 changed the coverage required when another driver causes a crash and has little or no insurance. While a passenger is in the rideshare vehicle, the required uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is now $60,000 per person and $300,000 per incident, down from $1 million. A separate $1 million liability requirement still applies when the rideshare driver causes a crash during the trip.

"Rideshare cases can be complicated because insurance coverage may depend on the driver's app status, the phase of the ride and who caused the crash," said Sanchez. "For Spanish-speaking families, those questions can feel even more overwhelming if no one explains the process clearly."

About Mendez & Sanchez, A.P.C.

Mendez & Sanchez represents individuals and families in serious injury and civil litigation matters in Southern California, Nevada and Honduras. The firm offers legal services in English and Spanish on a contingency-fee basis. It has handled more than 5,000 cases and recovered over $1 billion for clients. Learn more at www.mendezsanchezlaw.com.

data.title: Dow Jones Top Markets Headlines at 7 PM ET: U.S. Stocks Extend Plunge as AI Boom Turns to Bust | Trump ...
data.description:
U.S. Stocks Extend Plunge as AI Boom Turns to Bust

U.S. stocks plunged and an index of mega-cap technology stocks skirted bear-market territory as predictions of a speculative bust in artificial-intelligence stocks appeared to come to fruition.

----

Trump Says He Will Penalize Companies That Build Data Centers Outside the U.S.

The president said the move was meant to encourage the construction of the facilities in the U.S. to better compete with China on AI.

----

Fed Governor Lisa Cook Says Her October Dissent Reflected Inflation Fight's Urgency

The comments come as Cook is battling President Trump's attempts to fire her.

----

After Brexit, Britain's Government Floats 'Breturn'

The U.K.'s European psychodrama is about to return as Prime Minister Andy Burnham kick-starts a debate on rejoining the EU.

----

Fed Officials Are Chatting Up a Storm. Investors Are in the Dark About Their Plans.

The Federal Reserve is almost certain to raise interest rates next month to cool inflation. But the size of the increase is anyone's guess.

----

Consumer Sentiment Climbed in November

Consumer sentiment improved in November, according to the University of Michigan's monthly survey, yet it remains near historically low levels that reflect Americans' widespread economic frustrations.

----

The Fear Gauge Hit 40. This Is What the Market Is Worried About.

Investors no longer believe the AI bull case. They fear an unwinding is coming.

----

Canada Retail Sales Pull Back After 0.8% Rise in September

Canadian retail sales are heading for the sharpest drop in more than a year and a half, a possible sign of cracks in the resilience of household spending and slowing momentum for the economy.

----

China's AI Firms Are Addicted to Nvidia Chips. Now They Are Facing Withdrawal.

The move by the U.S. to cut off Chinese access to high-end computing power has dealt a blow to Beijing's artificial-intelligence ambitions.

----

U.K. Government Borrowed More in October, But Is on Track for Smaller Deficit

At 3.5% of gross domestic product, the budget deficit for the fiscal year to October was lower than the 3.8% recorded a year earlier.

----

Japan Consumer Inflation Reinforces Rate-Hike Expectations

Consumer prices excluding fresh food climbed 2.2% in October from a year earlier, reinforcing expectations for another interest-rate increase by the central bank.

----

Spain Remains Europe's Star Economy. Why Don't People Feel Richer?

Spain's economy continues to boast growth rates that are the envy of Europe. But as discontent continues to mount over living standards ahead of next week's elections, it is clear that not everyone is celebrating.

----

U.K. Consumer Confidence Picks Up Despite Rising Headwinds

Consumer sentiment recovered slightly, though inflation concerns and higher interest rates are set to continue weighing on household budgets in the coming months.

----

Eurozone Wage Growth Accelerates, But Remains Modest

Negotiated wage growth accelerated to 2.57% in the third quarter from 2.45% in the previous quarter, according to the ECB.

----

Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Flash PMI Data to Provide Gauge on Economic Growth

November's flash purchasing managers' surveys for the U.S., eurozone and U.K. could signal whether there is scope for the central banks to raise interest rates further.
